text:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change yesterday I’m seeing a sizable drop in prefix cache hit-rate for multi-tenant workloads. quick summary: global hit-rate down from ~72% -> ~54% on 8k seq traces. :thinking:
jorge: ugh. saw CI perf alert too. any idea whether it’s keying or warmup behavior?
sasha: did you repro on staging with the same batching heuristics?
maya: yes, repro on staging. I ran a focused trace on a 5k qps tenant mix. Root cause looks like some prefix normalization differences + the kernel change caused slightly different tokenization boundaries for the same user prompts, so many earlier cache entries don't match.
keisha: wait — tokenization boundaries? that would change prefix hashes. is this the new fast-subword patch?
maya: exactly. It uses the new token splicing optimization. For short prefixes it’s fine, but with long prompts the splice sometimes collapses a split we had relied on for deterministic prefix hashing.
jorge: can you paste the key derivation we use today?
maya: sure — current (simplified):
```
cache_key = sha256(tenant_id || model_id || quant_tag || prefix_normalized)
```
where prefix_normalized is tokenization -> remove trailing whitespace -> join tokens.
sasha: so tokenization variance will flip prefix_normalized. two problems: 1) cross-tenant collisions if tenant_id gets dropped somewhere, 2) small tokenization diffs cause cache churn.
keisha: we should consider adding a stable logical normalization that doesn’t depend on tokenizer internals. maybe normalize on raw utf8 chars and whitespace collapse before tokenizing. cheaper to compute too.
maya: we tried whitespace-collapse pre-tokenize, hit-rate improved ~6% but not back to baseline. I also profiled the warmup path to see KV read latency distribution. short log snippet: 
```
[perf] kv.lookup(ok)=135ms, read_hits=42%, cold_reads=58%
[pprof] cpu: kernel_select 32%, kv_decode 18%, network 12%
```
jorge: 135ms for kv.lookup seems high — is that tail from decryption?
maya: maybe. We currently encrypt cache entries at rest with a per-region AES key. Decrypt is handled in the runtime worker after fetch. pprof indicates AES-GCM unwrap ~6-8ms per entry on cpu-bound hosts. For batched lookups that adds up.
keisha: we could switch to HMACed opaque keys (store encrypted payload separately) so lookup only uses deterministic HMAC(tenant_salt, key) without decrypting payload to check TTL. That would keep privacy and reduce decrypt ops on misses.
sasha: but HMAC requires we store tenant_salt server-side — that’s fine. Concern: auditability — audit-bot, any constraints on storing HMACs vs fully encrypted entries?
audit-bot: storing HMACs is OK from an audit perspective if salt rotation and KMS access are logged. Ensure we retain deterministic mapping audit records for 90 days. Also confirm we don’t make HMAC values reversible.
jorge: also need to check cross-tenant key-space collisions if we change scheme. Do we have a collision scan?
maya: ran a quick simulation: 10M entries across 300 tenants, current scheme collision ~0.002%. If we switch to tenant-salted HMAC with 128-bit output the collision becomes statistically negligible.
keisha: operational tradeoff: salted HMAC means indices grow (can't dedupe across tenants) which is what we want. But we must also update cache warmup: warmup currently primes based on LRU routes aggregated without tenant scoping; that would waste memory across tenant-siloed keys.
sasha: warmup should be tenant-aware. Proposal: change warmup job to prefetch top-N per-tenant from request traces (configurable cap) rather than global top-N. That keeps total prefetch cost bounded.
jorge: good. timeline? is this small patch or bigger refactor?
maya: work-breakdown:
1) short-term mitigation: revert tokenizer splice for production model family (hotfix) — 1 day.
2) medium: change cache keying -> tenant-salted HMAC + normalization on raw text (no tokenizer op) — 3 days dev + 2 days canary.
3) batch: tenant-aware warmup + metrics (per-tenant hit-rate dashboards) — 1 sprint.
keisha: note: medium change needs migration plan. keys stored now are sha256 raw keys. we should support lookup fallback: on miss, try legacy key -> if hit, re-insert under new HMAC key so gradual migration.
maya: yep implemented fallback flow in a dev branch. pseudocode: 
```
val = kv.get(hmac_key)
if val == nil:
  old = kv.get(legacy_key)
  if old != nil:
    kv.put(hmac_key, old)
```
This avoids mass backfill.
sasha: regarding perf: we should also measure kernel selection CPU distribution post-change because the kernel patch moved some ops into userland which may affect decrypt concurrency. If decrypts are blocking, maybe we should offload decrypt to dedicated IO threads.
jorge: good point. Also add a metric for decrypt_count and decrypt_latency per-request so we can alert when decrypts > threshold.
keisha: security question: if we adopt tenant-salted HMAC, do we risk leaking tenant activity via cache key cardinality? telemetry shows keys count per-tenant is visible only internally, but external attackers have no access. still, limit metadata exposure in metrics we emit to product.
audit-bot: add requirement: any metric that could be used to infer tenant-specific usage must go through privacy review. Recommend noise addition or rollup at org-level for public dashboards.
maya: I’ll push the hotfix revert and start medium branch. I’ll also attach staging perf traces.
jorge: thanks. can you post a short repro guide in the branch PR so SRE can run the warmup job and compare hit curves? :thumbsup:
keisha: I’ll coordinate warmup job changes and add tenant caps.
sasha: I’ll add decrypt metrics and kitchen-sink pprof snapshots for next run.
audit-bot: Recorded action items: hotfix revert, HMAC keying design doc, warmup change, decrypt metrics. Audit will review HMAC design within 48h.
maya: thanks all. looping in @eng-security if needed — I’ll share design doc link once PR opened. :eyes:
